newsitem.title: DUBAI: Records to crumble at UAE's 25th birthday bash.
newsitem.headline: Records to crumble at UAE's 25th birthday bash.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates celebrated its 25th birthday on Monday with extravaganza which organisers boasted would break a series of world records.

As foreign dignitaries and cables of congratulations arrived in the Gulf oil state, the UAE revelled in the festivities commemorating its rags-to-riches transformation from a string of fishing villages to one of the world's wealthiest states.
In Dubai, the country's commercial centre, a main street was closed to traffic for several hours for the presentation of a 73-tonne cake.
"The cake is 2,530 metres (1.57 miles) long and weighs approximately 73,000 kg (160,000 lb)," chef Uwe Micheel of Dubai's Intercontinental Hotel said.
"It's about 12,000 kg (26,000 lb) more than we expected because the 28 hotels contributing baked more than necessary to break the world record," he said.

In the UAE's capital Abu Dhabi, organisers offered President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan what they called "the world's biggest bouquet", a monumental flower arrangement covering an area of about 45 square metres (484 square feet).
An estimated 5.5 million light bulbs and 45,000 national flags were fixed along the main streets of Abu Dhabi or draped on buildings along the sleek seaside skyline.
A 2,800 kg (6,200 lb) fibreglass falcon -- the UAE's national symbol -- was specially built to spread its wings over a palm-lined boulevard, newspapers said.
Dubai has spent an estimated 500,000 dirhams ($135,000) decorating the bustling metropolis. Students marched along the Sheikh Zaid highway holding aloft a 1,200 metre (0.7 mile) flag.
The Dubai Chamber of Commerce and Industry hoped to break another world record with what it said was the world's biggest photographic image of the world gracing its glass facade.
The UAE's population was getting decked out too. One Dubai beauty salon offered special deals to paint ladies' fingernails in the country's green, white, red and black national colours.
